mcp.note: The real tools/list + prompts/list payload an MCP client receives. ALL tool schemas ride in the agent context EVERY model turn (standing per-turn tax). Inspector-verifiable.

tools.name: briefing
tools.title: Briefing
tools.description: Structured session orientation: open/overdue commitments, blockers, stale candidates, recent decisions, preferences. Requires an explicit selector (scope, project, or all) — no unfiltered default. A PROJECT selector only matches commitments/blockers written WITH that project; a NULL-project memory never appears in a project briefing (issue #244). Active blockers leave this set when resolved (resolve archives the blocker memory). brief mode (default) returns counts plus top items; full returns the bounded lists.

tools.name: configure_scope
tools.title: Configure Scope
tools.description: Manage your memory scopes: list, create, rename, set aliases, or delete (registry only — existing memories keep their scope). Mutating actions require the write scope.

tools.name: describe_environment
tools.title: Describe Environment
tools.description: Report server capabilities (tool names, count, version), your registered scopes, and bounded memory/commitment counts. Exposes no secrets or configuration values.

tools.name: get_facts
tools.title: Get Facts
tools.description: Currently-valid facts for a subject, with optional bi-temporal time travel. List mode (no subject) returns the most recent facts, bounded by an optional limit (default 50, max 200).

tools.name: get_memories
tools.title: Get Memories
tools.description: Fetch the full content of memories by id — use this after search or handoff returns an item with truncated: true to read the complete body. Accepts up to 20 ids plus an optional maxContentChars per-item bound (default 10000, max 65536; ids × maxContentChars may not exceed 262144 per call); an item still truncated at the cap reports truncated: true with its full contentLength. Ids that do not resolve for you are listed in notFound — never an error.

tools.name: handoff
tools.title: Handoff
tools.description: Export structured context (decisions, open commitments, preferences — with content) for another agent or provider to pick up the thread. Requires an explicit selector (scope, project, or all); the payload is bounded. Item content is a bounded excerpt — when a line reports truncated: true, call get_memories with its id to read the full content.

tools.name: remember
tools.title: Remember
tools.description: Append a new memory (decision, fact, preference, blocker, commitment, ...). Never merges; append-only. Content is capped at 2000 characters. To surface a commitment or blocker in a PROJECT-scoped briefing, pass `project` — a memory written with a NULL project never matches a project filter (issue #244).

tools.name: resolve
tools.title: Resolve
tools.description: Settle a memory by its id. A commitment transitions to a target status (open, waiting, resolved, expired) — serves resolve and unresolve (resolved -> open); illegal transitions are rejected. A blocker is archived (status active -> archived) and leaves the active-blocker briefing; the passed status is ignored for blockers and the result reports archived. Commitments AND blockers must be written WITH a project to be resolvable from a project-scoped briefing.

tools.name: review_proposals
tools.title: Review Proposals
tools.description: List consolidation proposals (optionally by status), reject one, or accept one (materializes the proposed edge; a supersedes/updates edge also closes the predecessor). Reject and accept require the write scope.

tools.name: revise
tools.title: Revise
tools.description: Supersede an existing memory with a corrected successor, linked by a typed edge (supersedes or updates). Never edits in place; append-and-supersede.

tools.name: search
tools.title: Search
tools.description: Unified semantic + keyword retrieval over your memories, supersession-aware. Accepts a query and an optional result limit, plus optional filters that narrow the candidate set BEFORE fusion (no change to ranking weights): memoryType OR memoryTypes (a list of types, mutually exclusive with memoryType), scope, project, status, asOf (bi-temporal time travel with validAt/asKnownAt), and recordedAfter/recordedBefore (an inclusive recorded-at range over the live view — not time travel). Omit a filter to leave that axis unconstrained. Hit content is a bounded excerpt — when a hit reports truncated: true, call get_memories with its id to read the full content. To page: pass nextCursor back as cursor with the SAME query and filters; pages come from the ordering frozen on the first page, so a mid-walk write or archive can never duplicate or skip a hit. The cursor is bound to the query and filters that issued it: passing it with a changed query or filters is rejected as invalid input — omit the cursor to start a new search. The cursor token is a real context cost (~4-6 KB — it carries the frozen ids+scores of the candidate pool), so page only when you actually need more hits. Paging stops at the frozen pool: hasMore: false means the pool is exhausted — refine the query (better filters, more specific terms) instead of paging harder. For broad scans set projection: "compact" to omit content/contentLength/truncated per hit (~5x fewer tokens), then batch-fetch the interesting ids with get_memories.

memoryType.description: Single memory type to match. Mutually exclusive with memoryTypes — pass one or the other, never both.

memoryTypes.description: OR-set of memory types to match. Mutually exclusive with memoryType — pass one or the other, never both.

recordedAfter.description: Inclusive lower bound on recorded_at. Must not be later than recordedBefore when both are given.

recordedBefore.description: Inclusive upper bound on recorded_at. Must not be earlier than recordedAfter when both are given.

cursor.description: Opaque continuation token from a previous page’s nextCursor. Omit for the first page. Keep query and filters identical across pages of one walk.

projection.description: Per-hit output shape: full (default) includes the content excerpt; compact omits content/contentLength/truncated for cheap broad scans — batch-fetch interesting ids with get_memories.

prompts.name: briefing
prompts.title: Session briefing
prompts.description: Orient yourself at the start of a session: call the briefing TOOL with an explicit selector (no unfiltered default) to surface open/overdue commitments, blockers, stale candidates, recent decisions, and preferences.

arguments.name: selector
arguments.description: Which slice to brief over: a single scope, a single project, or all memories.

arguments.name: mode
arguments.description: brief (counts + top items, the default) or full (the bounded lists).

prompts.name: debrief
prompts.title: Session debrief
prompts.description: Close a session cleanly: review what happened, then persist what is worth keeping — decisions, commitments, and follow-ups — by calling the remember TOOL for each, and resolve any completed commitments.

arguments.name: scope
arguments.description: Optional scope (kebab-case, e.g. work, personal) the session belonged to.

cli.note: The CLI help an agent learns ONCE on demand (it already knows bash). Not re-sent per turn.
cli.help:
usage: 3ngram <command> [options]

commands:
  remember  --type <t> --topic <t> --content <c> [--scope --project --tags]
  search    <query> [--limit --type --scope --project --status]
  facts     [--subject --predicate --valid-at --as-known-at --limit]

global:  --base-url <url> --api-key <key> --json
env:     THREENGRAM_BASE_URL THREENGRAM_API_KEY (flags override)

commands.remember:
3ngram remember --type <type> --topic <topic> --content <content> [--scope <scope>] [--project <project>] [--tags <tag>]... [--base-url <url>] [--api-key <key>] [--json]
  Append a new memory (decision, fact, preference, ...). --type/--topic/--content required.
commands.search:
3ngram search <query> [--limit <n>] [--type <type>] [--scope <scope>] [--project <project>] [--status <status>] [--base-url <url>] [--api-key <key>] [--json]
  Unified semantic + keyword retrieval. Query is positional or --query.
commands.facts:
3ngram facts [--subject <subject>] [--predicate <predicate>] [--valid-at <iso>] [--as-known-at <iso>] [--limit <n>] [--base-url <url>] [--api-key <key>] [--json]
  Currently-valid facts for a subject, with optional bi-temporal time travel.
